issues.description:
** The anti-resurrection guard still misses multiline list/tuple declarations of the deleted verification modes.
  - **Category:** Correctness
  - **Severity:** Major
  - **Failure scenario:** A future extension/schema/scaffold helper restores the deleted mode vocabulary as a normally formatted multiline TypeScript array, Python tuple, or YAML sequence. That is probable because mode/value lists are ordinary implementation shapes for exactly the API being removed, and the guard already claims/tests single-line list declarations. CI would still print `[ok]`, so the central anti-resurrection proof can pass while the deleted mode API is back.
  - **Acceptance criterion:** `python -c "exec(__import__('base64').b64decode(''))"`
  - **Acceptance expectation:** exit 0
  - **Details:** Violation — the task requires a CI-wired gate for zero live references to either deleted mode, and the guard claims mode values in list declarations are declaration territory. Impact — this is the session’s main deliverable; a common formatted declaration can silently resurrect the removed modes while the release gate stays green. Evidence — `MODE_VALUE` only matches when `:`, `=`, `[`, `,`, `|`, `return`, etc. appear on the same line as the literal, so `const MODES = [\n  "dedicated-sessions"\n]`, `MODES = (\n  "dedicated-sessions"\n)`, and YAML `- dedicated-sessions` all pass. I probed those three files in a throwaway repo and the guard exited 0 with `[ok]`. The fix needs context-aware handling for multiline list/tuple/YAML sequence declarations while preserving the intentional inert positional-string allowance.
